items.title: Russia, Ukraine trade thousands of violation claims as Easter ceasefire crumbles

featured_image.name: ‘Easter truce’ in Russia’s Ukraine war marked by accusations of violations

items.description: A 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine fell apart within hours of taking effect, with both sides accusing each other of thousands of breaches by Sunday morning. The truce, declared by Russian President Vladimir Putin on April 9 and effective from 4 p.m. on Saturday, was intended to cover the Easter holiday through the end of Sunday.[1][2]

items.title: IRGC claims full control of Strait of Hormuz after Trump orders blockade

featured_image.name: Trump threatens Strait of Hormuz blockade after US-Iran ceasefire talks end without agreement

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared on Sunday that its naval forces have assumed full control over all maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, issuing a sharp warning to Washington just hours after President Trump announced a U.S. naval blockade of the critical waterway.

In a statement posted in Persian on X, accompanied by video footage appearing to show vessels targeted in crosshairs, the IRGC naval command said "all traffic is under the full control of the armed forces" and warned that "the enemy will become trapped in a deadly vortex in the Strait if it makes the wrong move". The declaration came as a direct response to Trump's announcement on Truth Social that the U.S. Navy would "effective immediately" begin blockading all ships attempting to enter or leave the strait.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Chinese crystal breaks record in race to build nuclear clocks

featured_image.name: Scientists develop new ammonium fluorooxoborate crystal - CGTN

items.description:
Scientists in China have created the world's first crystal capable of producing the ultraviolet light needed to power thorium nuclear clocks, a development that could one day enable submarines and deep-space probes to navigate without GPS.

The fluorinated borate compound, developed by a team led by Pan Shilie at the Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry, can push laser light down to a record 145.2 nanometres — short enough to meet a critical requirement for these ultra-precise, compact timekeepers, the South China Morning Post reported. The research was published in the journal Advanced Materials earlier this year.[1][2]

items.title: Hungarians vote in election that could end Orban's 16-year rule

featured_image.name: Hungary Holds Parliamentary Elections

items.description:
Hungarians are voting on Sunday in a parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Viktor Orban's 16-year grip on power, with record-high turnout reported in the early hours and opposition challenger Peter Magyar's Tisza party leading in most opinion polls.[1][2][3]

Polling stations opened at 6 a.m. local time and are set to close at 7 p.m., with roughly 8 million citizens eligible to elect the 199 members of the National Assembly. By 11 a.m., turnout had reached 37.98% — the highest ever recorded at that hour and about 12 percentage points above the same point in the 2022 election, according to Hungary's National Election Office. High turnout is widely seen as favoring the opposition.[4][3][5][1]

items.title: Trump orders naval blockade of Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump announces naval blockade on Iran after peace talks ...

items.description:
President Trump announced on Sunday that the US Navy would immediately begin blockading all ships entering or leaving the Strait of Hormuz, a sharp escalation that came just hours after marathon peace talks with Iran in Islamabad ended without a deal.

"Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social, according to CBS News. He said the Navy would also "seek and interdict every vessel in International Waters that has paid a toll to Iran" and begin destroying mines Iran had laid in the waterway. "Any Iranian who fires at us, or at peaceful vessels, will be BLOWN TO HELL!" he added.[1][2]

items.title: Putin offers to mediate after US-Iran talks collapse in Islamabad

featured_image.name: Russia seeks to serve as mediator between US and Iran

items.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Sunday that Moscow stands ready to mediate between the United States and Iran, hours after marathon negotiations in Islamabad ended without an agreement and raised fears that a fragile ceasefire could unravel.

"Vladimir Putin emphasized his readiness to further facilitate the search for a political and diplomatic settlement to the conflict, and to mediate efforts to achieve a just and lasting peace in the Middle East," the Kremlin said in its readout of the call.[1][2]

items.title: Study finds three distinct types of black hole mergers

featured_image.name: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA detect most massive black hole merger to ...

items.description: A team of astrophysicists has found that merging black holes detected through gravitational waves do not all form the same way. Instead, they fall into three distinct subpopulations, each bearing the fingerprints of a different cosmic origin story. The study, submitted to the preprint server arXiv on March 18, draws on data from the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration's latest gravitational-wave catalog, which now contains over 150 confirmed binary black hole detections.[1][2]

items.title: Iran lost track of its own mines in Hormuz, NYT reports

featured_image.name: Iran Mines Strait of Hormuz and the US Navy Cannot Clear It

items.description: A desperate race for crude oil is gripping global markets as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut more than six weeks after Iran closed the waterway in retaliation for the US-Israeli air campaign launched on 28 February. Physical oil prices have surged to record levels, refiners across Asia and Europe are slashing output, and a two-week ceasefire announced on 7 April has done little to restore normal shipping through the world's most critical energy chokepoint.

items.title: Economists say world far better equipped for oil shocks than in the 1970s

featured_image.name: Gas Lines Evoke Memories Of Oil Crises In The 1970s : The ...

items.description: The Middle East conflict that has sent oil prices surging in recent months has revived memories of the 1970s energy crises, yet economists say the United States and other major economies are far better equipped to weather the storm today than they were five decades ago, according to an analysis by the Associated Press.[1]

items.title: USS John P. Murtha returns to San Diego with Artemis II Orion capsule

featured_image.name: Artemis II makes 'perfect' splashdown after historic mission

items.description: The amphibious transport dock USS John P. Murtha (LPD 26) returned to Naval Base San Diego on Saturday morning carrying NASA's Orion capsule after recovering the spacecraft and its four-person crew from the Pacific Ocean following the Artemis II lunar mission.[1][2]

items.title: China unveils 10 incentives for Taiwan after historic Xi-Cheng meeting

featured_image.name: China's Xi meets Taiwan opposition leader ahead of key ...

items.description: China on Sunday announced a package of 10 policy measures aimed at boosting cross-strait exchanges with Taiwan, capping a historic visit by Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun that included the first meeting between leaders of the KMT and the Chinese Communist Party in nearly a decade.

items.title: UK shelves Chagos Islands handover after Trump opposition

featured_image.name: Trump is right: The UK Chagos deal is an 'act of great stupidity'

items.description:
The United Kingdom announced on Saturday that it has put on hold its plan to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, acknowledging that the deal cannot proceed without the backing of the United States, which President Donald Trump has withheld.

The bill underpinning the agreement has been pulled from the upcoming King's Speech, where the government's legislative agenda for the next parliamentary session will be set out in May, according to Sky News. The legislation had been working its way through Parliament but ran out of time, and officials confirmed it will not be reintroduced in the next session.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump warns China of 'big problems' over Iran arms

featured_image.name: Trump Reacts to China Reportedly Preparing to Ship Weapons to Iran

items.description: President Trump warned on Saturday that China would face "big problems" if it supplies weapons to Iran, sharpening the economic and geopolitical standoff between Washington and Beijing even as the two nations navigate fragile ceasefire negotiations in the Middle East. The remarks, made to reporters as he departed the White House, came days after Trump threatened a blanket 50 percent tariff on imports from any country found arming Tehran.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: US-Iran talks collapse after 21 hours with no deal, Vance says

featured_image.name: Direct U.S.-Iran talks fail to reach resolution after ...

items.description:
Vice President JD Vance announced early Sunday that marathon negotiations between the United States and Iran ended without a peace agreement after 21 hours of talks in Islamabad, Pakistan, with Tehran refusing to accept American demands on nuclear non-proliferation. Vance said Washington had been "quite flexible" but did not receive an "affirmative commitment" from Iran on abandoning its nuclear ambitions.[1][2][3]

The breakdown came after the highest-level face-to-face engagement between American and Iranian leaders since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. Vance led the U.S. delegation alongside special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law, while Iran's delegation was headed by parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Pakistan mediated the trilateral discussions, which began Saturday afternoon local time and stretched past dawn Sunday.[4][5]

items.title: Qatar resumes full maritime navigation Sunday amid Gulf ceasefire

featured_image.name: Qatar's ports play pivotal role in strengthening country's ...

items.description: Qatar's Ministry of Transport announced on Friday the full resumption of maritime navigation for all types of vessels and ships beginning Sunday, April 12, 2026, marking a return to broader normalcy after weeks of restrictions tied to the regional military crisis.[1][2][3]

items.title: Lebanon death toll passes 2,000 as Israel-Hezbollah fighting intensifies

featured_image.name: Hezbollah rockets target Israel’s north as Israel pounds Beirut suburbs

items.description:
Lebanon's Health Ministry confirmed Saturday that at least 2,020 people have been killed and 6,436 wounded since the country was drawn into the broader U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran on March 2, as Israeli forces showed no signs of halting operations against Hezbollah despite ongoing ceasefire negotiations between Washington and Tehran.[1][2]

The grim milestone came as the Israel Defense Forces reported striking approximately 200 Hezbollah targets across Lebanon overnight Friday and into Saturday, hitting what it described as terror infrastructure and rocket launchers in support of ground operations in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah, meanwhile, continued to fire rockets and drones into northern Israel, with sirens sounding across the Galilee region and a rocket striking the city of Safed on Thursday, injuring several people.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Trump says 'we win' regardless of Iran talks outcome

featured_image.name: US President Trump says US 'wins' regardless of how Iran talks go

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that the outcome of historic peace talks with Iran is of no consequence to the United States, telling reporters outside the White House that "whether we make a deal or not makes no difference to me" because "regardless of what happens, we win."[1][2]

His remarks came as Vice President JD Vance led hours of negotiations with Iranian officials in Islamabad, Pakistan — the first direct high-level talks between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.[3][4]

items.title: Netanyahu says Iran has no functioning enrichment facilities left

featured_image.name: Read Netanyahu's full statement on Iran attacks | PBS News

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared on Saturday that the joint U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran had succeeded in "crushing" the Islamic republic's nuclear and ballistic missile programs, even as he insisted the war was far from over.[1]

In a televised statement delivered as Iranian and American officials held a second round of face-to-face peace talks in Islamabad, Pakistan, Netanyahu claimed "enormous achievements" while warning that Israel reserves the right to resume hostilities at any time.[2][1]

items.title: Pope Leo XIV decries 'delusion of omnipotence' fueling Iran war

featured_image.name: Pope Leo XIV denounces the 'delusion of omnipotence' he says ...

items.description:
Pope Leo XIV delivered his sharpest condemnation yet of the U.S.-Israel war in Iran on Saturday, presiding over an evening prayer vigil at St. Peter's Basilica where he denounced the "delusion of omnipotence" driving the conflict and demanded world leaders choose negotiation over military force.

The vigil, which featured Scripture readings and meditative recitation of Rosary prayers, coincided with the start of historic face-to-face peace talks between the United States and Iran in Islamabad, Pakistan — the first direct dialogue between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.[1]

items.title: Netanyahu says Israel's Iran campaign 'not over' as U.S.-Iran talks begin in Islamabad

featured_image.name: Netanyahu says campaign against Iran 'not over,' admits ...

items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared Saturday night that Israel's campaign against Iran "is not over," issuing a video statement that touted what he called "historic achievements" while acknowledging that "we still have more to do," even as U.S. and Iranian negotiators held their first round of ceasefire talks in Islamabad.[1][2]
